title: Maple and Hugo's Sleepy Song
markdown:
The sky was wearing its softest blue pajamas, and shy stars peeked out, twinkling like spilled sugar. Maple the marmalade cat, fur warm as sunshine, stretched a soft paw. Her claws stayed tucked inside. “Oh, Hugo,” she purred, her voice a low rumble. “The pond is getting so still and quiet.”

Hugo the hedgehog nodded his sleepy head. His nose twitched. “Yes, Maple,” he hummed, his voice a gentle stream sound. “The ducks will want their sleepy song. Shall we sing it for them? It’s our favourite job.”

“Oh, yes please,” whispered Maple, her tail swishing slow and happy. So, together, the two friends padded softly, ever so softly, to the whispering pond. Maple’s paws made no sound on the mossy path. Hugo’s little feet rustled ever so gently through fallen leaves that whispered secrets. The air smelled like cool damp grass and sweet night flowers. A little owl hooted a soft hoo-hoo, a gentle question. Crickets began their quiet chirping, a soft hum of little lullabies.

When they reached the pond, the water lay like a dark shimmering mirror. It perfectly reflected the pearly moon climbing higher. The ducks were nestled together in cosy hollows. Their soft feathers were tucked in. They looked very, very peaceful. Maple and Hugo stood very, very still. They did not want to disturb the quiet magic. Then, in voices as soft as dandelion fluff, they began to sing their special sleepy song.

Maple hummed a sweet flowing tune, like a gentle river. Hugo added his gentle harmony, a sound like soft pebbles in the river. Their sleepy song flowed over the water. It was a soft comforting wave.

“Sleepy ducks, sleepy pond,
Moonbeams soft and fond.
Hush now, rest your little heads,
Dream of yummy watery beds.
Feathers soft and water deep,
Now it’s time for you to sleep.”

As they sang their gentle song, a deep quiet settled over everything. The water seemed to sigh. The tall reeds swayed, nodding along. The ducks’ eyes stayed closed. They listened to the sweet calming sounds. It felt like a warm blanket. The whole world seemed to listen to the gentle song that promised sweet dreams.

When the last soft note faded, the pond was perfectly still. Not a ripple disturbed the glassy surface. Moonbeams danced softly on the water. Maple and Hugo looked at each other. Their eyes felt heavy. Their own song had brought them lovely warm sleepiness. They felt wonderfully drowsy. They were ready for their own cosy adventures.

“That was a lovely song, Hugo,” yawned Maple. Her tail swished slow and sleepy.

“It was,” agreed Hugo. His little nose wiggled as he yawned too. A tiny sleepy eep escaped him. “And now, I think it’s time for us to find our cosy spots for dreaming. My prickles feel ready for a snuggle.”

They turned away from the silent pond. They felt warm and safe and content. They were ready for lovely sleepy adventures. Soon, with soft sighs and happy little snuffles, they both drifted off into peaceful slumber. Their hearts were full of the quiet joy of a song well sung.

And so a sleepy song, shared with a friend, tucks the singers in as softly as the ducks.
